newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on rain in spring wheat area.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on rain in spring wheat area.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on rains in the U.S. spring wheat growing region and new crop July hit a four-month low, traders said.
Traders and analysts also cited the lack of large scale export business as bearish to the market.

"This $3.50 area (in the July wheat) was a major demand area for the bulls but it failed to elicit much support," said John Kleist, director of research for ING Futures and Options. "That is probably hurting wheat more than the rain. Anticipated demand just did not materialize."
There were weekend rains in the upper Midwest and Plains.

The rains was especially important in North Dakota, a key U.S. spring wheat growing state, traders said. Dry weather in the spring wheat states had been causing concern about reductions in yield prospects.

"I think it's that (rains in spring wheat areas) and I think that even though we have competitive prices, they wanted to see better sales (export) activity," said Dan Cekander, analyst for FIMAT Futures.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 10-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 9-3/4 at $3.42-3/4.
Wheat also was pressured by seasonal factors including active weekend harvesting in parts of the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat belt.
There were scattered showers overnight in some harvesting areas but the rainfall was not sufficient to sharply curtail the harvest.

Wheat futures may have been underpinned by export news, some3 sources noted. USDA Monday said U.S. wheat export inspections during the week ended June 12 totaled 14.425 million bushels, above expectations for 10 million to 12 million bushels.
Cargill Inc sold five million bushels of September and Continental Grain sold 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, below the 22,725 traded Friday.

In wheat options, Paine Webber bought 200 September $5.00 calls at 3/4 cent, Produce Grain sold 200 July $3.60 puts at 15 to 16 cents and FIMAT Futures sold 200 September $3.40 puts at 10 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 11,073 traded Friday.
